The disc brake is preferably actuated by compressed air and is designed for use in a motor vehicle, particularly in a commercial vehicle or another vehicle in which reliable, high-performance braking is required.

The brake caliper of the disc brake comprises a brake application section. This brake application section accommodates a brake application device, which is used to apply braking force to the brake pads. The brake application device includes a rotary brake lever by means of which an actuating force, for example from a pneumatic actuator, can be transmitted and converted into a brake application movement.

In order to compensate for wear of the brake pads during operation, the brake application section further includes at least one wear adjusting device. This wear adjusting device serves to adjust the position of the brake application mechanism as the brake pads become thinner, thereby maintaining a desired clearance between the brake pads and the brake disc and ensuring consistent braking performance.

A synchronization unit is provided for coordinating the adjustment movement. The synchronization unit includes an adjusting device, a drive device, and a synchronizer. The adjusting device performs the wear adjustment, while the drive device transmits or initiates the adjustment movement. The synchronizer ensures that the adjustment movement is transmitted in a coordinated manner, particularly when more than one adjusting element is present.

The adjusting device and the drive unit are inserted into threaded plungers of a spindle unit. These threaded plungers form part of the mechanism that converts rotary adjustment movement into axial displacement for compensating brake pad wear. The adjusting device and the drive unit are secured to a bearing wall of the brake application section by respective mounting arrangements. These mounting arrangements provide accurate positioning and reliable support of the components within the brake caliper.

The synchronization unit is preferably installed as a preassembled group into the brake application section. In this way, the adjusting device, the drive device, and the synchronizer can be assembled and tested before being inserted into the brake caliper, simplifying final assembly and improving reliability. When installed, the synchronizer is positioned near the mounting arrangements on the bearing wall, enabling a compact arrangement and effective synchronization of the adjusting components within the brake application section.
outputs.L4:
A compressed-air disc brake for a motor vehicle is provided, in particular for a commercial vehicle. The disc brake includes a brake caliper which straddles a brake disc and contains a brake application section. In the brake application section, a rotary brake lever is arranged for transmitting an actuating force, generated for example by a pneumatic brake cylinder, to the brake pads. The rotary brake lever acts on one or more threaded plunger spindle units which convert the lever movement into an axial application movement of the brake pads toward the brake disc.

To compensate for brake pad and brake disc wear, the disc brake is equipped with wear-adjusting devices. These devices ensure that, as friction material is worn away during operation, the clearance between the brake pads and the brake disc is restored to a desired value. The threaded plunger spindle units are therefore not only used to apply the brake force but also serve as adjustable elements for setting the correct brake clearance.

The wear-adjusting system is coupled by a synchronization unit. This synchronization unit comprises an adjusting device, a drive device, and a synchronizer. The adjusting device performs the adjustment movement, the drive device transmits the adjustment input from the brake application mechanism, and the synchronizer ensures that the threaded plunger spindle units are adjusted uniformly. In this way, both sides or both application points of the brake are kept in proper alignment, preventing uneven pad wear and ensuring reliable braking performance.

A particular feature of the brake is that the synchronization unit is designed as a preassembled group. Before being installed in the brake caliper, the adjusting device, drive device, and synchronizer are assembled together into a functional unit. This preassembled group can then be inserted into the brake application section of the brake caliper as a single module. This reduces the number of individual assembly steps required during manufacture and minimizes the risk of incorrect installation or misalignment of the individual components.

The synchronizer is arranged in the region of mounting arrangements formed on or near a bearing wall of the brake caliper. The bearing wall supports and positions essential parts of the brake application mechanism, including the rotary brake lever and associated bearing elements. By placing the synchronizer close to these mounting arrangements, the synchronization unit can be integrated compactly into the existing structure of the brake caliper. This arrangement also improves the mechanical support of the synchronizer and allows short, direct force and motion transmission paths between the adjusting components and the threaded plunger spindle units.

As a result, the compressed-air disc brake provides a robust and space-saving arrangement for automatic wear adjustment. The modular design of the synchronization unit simplifies production and assembly, while the positioning of the synchronizer near the bearing wall improves functional integration within the brake application section. The brake therefore offers reliable compensation for wear, uniform adjustment of the plunger spindle units, and efficient installation in a motor vehicle braking system.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” may be one of the smallest words in the English language, but it carries great importance. It is known as the definite article, used to point to a specific person, place, thing, or idea. When we say “the book,” we are not talking about just any book—we mean a particular one that the speaker and listener both understand.

This simple word helps make communication clear. Without “the,” sentences can sound vague or incomplete. For example, “I saw dog” feels unnatural, while “I saw the dog” tells us that the dog is specific and already known in the conversation.

“The” appears everywhere: in stories, conversations, news articles, songs, and everyday speech. It helps connect ideas and guide meaning. Although it is short and often unnoticed, “the” is one of the most useful and frequently used words in English.

In many ways, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have a big impact.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent abstract for a compressed-air actuated disc brake with a brake caliper, rotary brake lever, wear adjuster, threaded plungers, and a preassembled synchronization unit mounted on a bearing wall.
counterfactuals.output: A compressed-air actuated disc brake includes a brake caliper straddling a brake disc, a rotary brake lever actuable by a pneumatic actuator, and a brake application mechanism for pressing at least one brake pad against the brake disc. The rotary brake lever acts on at least one threaded plunger via an adjusting system configured to compensate for brake pad wear. A synchronization device couples a plurality of threaded plungers for coordinated adjustment. The synchronization device is formed as a preassembled synchronization unit mounted on a bearing wall of the brake caliper or of a caliper-side support structure. The unit includes synchronization elements arranged to transmit rotary motion between the threaded plungers and is positionable on the bearing wall before or during assembly of the brake application mechanism. This configuration simplifies assembly, improves alignment of the plungers and synchronization components, and provides reliable wear adjustment in a compact compressed-air disc brake construction.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a concise technical description of a vehicle disc brake including a brake application device, wear adjusting device, drive device, synchronizer, mounting arrangements, and an installation method for the synchronization unit.
counterfactuals.output:
A vehicle disc brake comprises a brake caliper arranged to straddle a brake disc and at least one brake application device for pressing a brake pad against the brake disc. The brake application device includes one or more rotatable adjusting spindles or thrust elements operatively connected to a wear adjusting device that compensates for lining and disc wear by advancing the brake pad toward the disc.

A drive device is coupled to the wear adjusting device and converts actuation or relative movement within the brake application mechanism into an adjusting rotation. A synchronizer is provided between multiple adjusting elements to ensure uniform adjustment. The synchronizer may include a synchronization unit, such as a chain, belt, gear train, or toothed coupling, which connects respective adjustment shafts or spindles so that rotation of one adjusting element is transmitted to the other.

The synchronization unit is supported by mounting arrangements on the brake caliper or on a carrier plate. These mounting arrangements define fixed bearing or guide positions for the synchronizer and maintain correct spacing, alignment, and tension between the coupled adjusting elements. The mounting arrangements may include receiving pockets, bearing seats, retaining clips, covers, or fastening points that allow the synchronization unit to be pre-positioned and secured relative to the brake application device.

An installation method for the synchronization unit includes positioning the synchronizer on the mounting arrangements before or during assembly of the brake application device, engaging the synchronizer with the respective drive or adjustment elements, and fixing it in its operating position by means of retainers or a cover. The method allows the synchronization unit to be installed as a preassembled module, aligned with the adjusting spindles, and secured without requiring later manual synchronization, thereby simplifying assembly and ensuring coordinated wear adjustment of the disc brake.

counterfactuals.output:
## Summary of the Invention

The invention relates to a disc brake caliper for a vehicle disc brake, in particular for a commercial vehicle, comprising a caliper body configured to straddle a brake disc and having a bearing wall on an actuation side of the caliper. The brake caliper includes a rotary brake lever mounted in the caliper body for applying an actuation force to at least one brake pad in the direction of the brake disc. The rotary brake lever is operatively connected to a synchronization unit for coordinating brake actuation and/or wear adjustment functions within the caliper.

The synchronization unit comprises an adjusting device, a drive device, and a synchronizer. The adjusting device is configured to compensate for brake pad and/or brake disc wear by adjusting a clearance between the brake pad and the brake disc. The drive device is operatively associated with the rotary brake lever and is configured to transmit rotational or pivoting movement generated during brake actuation to the adjusting device. The synchronizer is configured to synchronize adjustment movement between associated adjustment components, in particular between adjustment spindles or thrust elements arranged within the caliper.

According to the invention, the synchronization unit is arranged in the region of mounting arrangements provided on or adjacent to the bearing wall of the brake caliper. The mounting arrangements may serve to support, receive, or locate functional components of the brake actuation mechanism, including the rotary brake lever and/or elements of the synchronization unit. By positioning the adjusting device, drive device, and synchronizer near the mounting arrangements on the bearing wall, the caliper achieves a compact construction, improved structural integration, and reduced tolerance sensitivity between the lever mechanism and the adjustment system.

In one embodiment, the bearing wall comprises receiving formations, bearing seats, recesses, bosses, or fastening portions for supporting the rotary brake lever and at least part of the synchronization unit. The drive device may be positioned directly adjacent to the rotary brake lever so that lever movement can be efficiently transferred to the adjusting device. The synchronizer may extend between spaced adjustment components and may be located close to the bearing wall to reduce installation space and protect the synchronizing mechanism within the caliper body.

This arrangement provides a robust and space-saving brake caliper architecture in which the force application mechanism and wear adjustment mechanism are integrated in a common structural region of the caliper. The invention thereby facilitates simplified assembly, improved alignment of the synchronization components, reduced component loading, and enhanced reliability of automatic brake adjustment during service life.
